You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# thokr
✨ sleek typing tui with visualized results and historical logging

[![GitHub Build Workflow](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/build.yml)

[![Crate Version](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/thokr)](https://crates.io/crates/thokr)
[![Github Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/thatvegandev/thokr)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/stargazers)

![demo](https://github.com/thatvegandev/assets/raw/main/thokr/demo.gif)

## Usage

For detailed usage run `thokr -h`.

```
thokr 0.4.1
sleek typing tui with visualized results and historical logging

USAGE:
    thokr [OPTIONS]

OPTIONS:
    -f, --full-sentences <NUMBER_OF_SENTENCES>
            number of sentences to use in test

    -h, --help
            Print help information

    -l, --supported-language <SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE>
            language to pull words from [default: english] [possible values: english, english1k,
            english10k]

    -p, --prompt <PROMPT>
            custom prompt to use

    -s, --number-of-secs <NUMBER_OF_SECS>
            number of seconds to run test

    -V, --version
            Print version information

    -w, --number-of-words <NUMBER_OF_WORDS>
            number of words to use in test [default: 15]

```


## Installation

### Cargo

```sh
$ cargo install thokr
```

### Docker

```sh
$ docker run -it thatvegandev/thokr
```

### Arch Linux

Install `thokr-git` from the AUR

## Usage

For detailed usage run `thokr -h`.

### Examples

| command                     |                                                    test contents |
|:----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------:|
| `thokr`                     |                          50 of the 200 most common english words |
| `thokr -w 100`              |                         100 of the 200 most common English words |
| `thokr -w 100 -l english1k` |                        100 of the 1000 most common English words |
| `thokr -w 10 -s 5`          | 10 of the 200 most common English words (hard stop at 5 seconds) |
| `thokr -p "$(cat foo.txt)"` |                   custom prompt with the output of `cat foo.txt` |
| `thokr -f 4`                | 4 grammatical sentences with full stops; overrides word settings |

_During a test you can press ← to start over or → to see a new prompt (assuming
you didn't supply a custom one)_

## Supported Languages

The following languages are available by default:

| name         |                     description |
| :----------- | ------------------------------: |
| `english`    |   200 most common English words |
| `english1k`  |  1000 most common English words |
| `english10k` | 10000 most common English words |

## Logging

Upon completion of a test, a row outlining your results is appended to the
`log.csv` file found in the following platform-specific folders. This way you
can easily track your progress over time.

| platform | value                                                            |                                        example |
| :------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------: |
| Linux    | $XDG*CONFIG_HOME/\_project_path* or $HOME/.config/_project_path_ |                      /home/colby/.config/thokr |
| macOS    | $HOME/Library/Application Support/_project_path_                 | /Users/Colby/Library/Application Support/thokr |
| Windows  | {FOLDERID*RoamingAppData}\_project_path*\config                  |    C:\Users\Colby\AppData\Roaming\thokr\config |

# thokr
✨ sleek typing tui with visualized results and historical logging

[![GitHub Build Workflow](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/build.yml)
[![GitHub Deploy Workflow](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/deploy.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/deploy.yml)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-default.svg)](./LICENSE.md)
[![Crate Version](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/thokr)](https://crates.io/crates/thokr)
[![Github Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/thatvegandev/thokr)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/stargazers)

![demo](https://github.com/thatvegandev/assets/raw/main/thokr/demo.gif)

## Usage

For detailed usage run `thokr -h`.

```
thokr 0.4.1
sleek typing tui with visualized results and historical logging

USAGE:
    thokr [OPTIONS]

OPTIONS:
    -f, --full-sentences <NUMBER_OF_SENTENCES>
            number of sentences to use in test

    -h, --help
            Print help information

    -l, --supported-language <SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE>
            language to pull words from [default: english] [possible values: english, english1k,
            english10k]

    -p, --prompt <PROMPT>
            custom prompt to use

    -s, --number-of-secs <NUMBER_OF_SECS>
            number of seconds to run test

    -V, --version
            Print version information

    -w, --number-of-words <NUMBER_OF_WORDS>
            number of words to use in test [default: 15]

```


## Installation

### Cargo

```sh
$ cargo install thokr
```

### Docker

```sh
$ docker run -it thatvegandev/thokr
```

### Arch Linux

Install `thokr-git` from the AUR

## Usage

For detailed usage run `thokr -h`.

### Examples

| command                     |                                                    test contents |
|:----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------:|
| `thokr`                     |                          50 of the 200 most common english words |
| `thokr -w 100`              |                         100 of the 200 most common English words |
| `thokr -w 100 -l english1k` |                        100 of the 1000 most common English words |
| `thokr -w 10 -s 5`          | 10 of the 200 most common English words (hard stop at 5 seconds) |
| `thokr -p "$(cat foo.txt)"` |                   custom prompt with the output of `cat foo.txt` |
| `thokr -f 4`                | 4 grammatical sentences with full stops; overrides word settings |

_During a test you can press ← to start over or → to see a new prompt (assuming
you didn't supply a custom one)_

## Supported Languages

The following languages are available by default:

| name         |                     description |
| :----------- | ------------------------------: |
| `english`    |   200 most common English words |
| `english1k`  |  1000 most common English words |
| `english10k` | 10000 most common English words |

## Logging

Upon completion of a test, a row outlining your results is appended to the
`log.csv` file found in the following platform-specific folders. This way you
can easily track your progress over time.

| platform | value                                                            |                                        example |
| :------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------: |
| Linux    | $XDG*CONFIG_HOME/\_project_path* or $HOME/.config/_project_path_ |                      /home/colby/.config/thokr |
| macOS    | $HOME/Library/Application Support/_project_path_                 | /Users/Colby/Library/Application Support/thokr |
| Windows  | {FOLDERID*RoamingAppData}\_project_path*\config                  |    C:\Users\Colby\AppData\Roaming\thokr\config |

## Roadmap

- [ ] ⚡️ Performance
  - Right now there are known performance issues surrounding the rendering of
    the tui at each tick interval and/or key press. Ideally each render uses the
    prior render as a base and only makes the necessary adjustments (possibly
    using
    [StatefulWidget](https://docs.rs/tui/0.10.0/tui/widgets/trait.StatefulWidget.html)),
    but I haven't been able to figure that out yet.
- [ ] 🔠 Multi-language support
  - I decided not to launch thokr with languages besides english because of some
    odd rendering issues I was experiencing when trying to input characters with
    accents. It's as though I'm not able to properly input the character in [raw
    mode](https://docs.rs/crossterm/0.3.0/crossterm/raw/index.html). I'd love to
    have that figure out before shipping other languages because I personally
    felt the experience was a bit jarring. I'll open an bug report for it with
    more details and replication steps -- would love more eyes on that problem!
- [ ] 🧪 Tests
  - I've only written a small amount of tests at this point. I haven't sat down
    to really think through what tests look like when the output is dependent on
    the users terminal size, font size, etc. If you have any ideas for this please
    open up an issue and start the discussion!

## Contributing

All contributions are **greatly appreciated**.

If you have a suggestion that would make thokr better, please fork the repo and
create a [pull request](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/pulls). You can
also simply open an issue and select `Feature Request`

1. Fork the repo
2. Create your feature branch (`git checkout -b [your_username]/xyz`)
3. Commit your changes (`git commit -m 'add some xyz'`)
4. Rebase off main (`git fetch --all && git rebase origin/main`)
5. Push to your branch (`git push origin [your_username]/xyz`)
6. Fill out pull request template

See the [open issues](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/issues) for a full
list of proposed features (and known issues).

import subprocess, os, pty, select, time

# Test running under a pty to see TUI
import pty, os, subprocess, select, time

def run_pty(args, width=80, height=24, wait=2.0, send_keys=None):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    import struct, fcntl, termios
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", height, width, 0, 0))
    p = subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, close_fds=True)
    os.close(slave)
    time.sleep(wait)
    # try reading non-blocking
    import fcntl as fcntl2
    flags = fcntl2.fcntl(master, fcntl2.F_GETFL)
    fcntl2.fcntl(master, fcntl2.F_SETFL, flags | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    data=b""

import pty, os, subprocess, select, time, struct, fcntl, termios

def raw_session(prompt_args, keys=[], width=80, height=24):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", height, width, 0, 0))
    p = subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+prompt_args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, close_fds=True)
    os.close(slave)
    # nonblocking
    import fcntl as f2
    flags = f2.fcntl(master, f2.F_GETFL)
    f2.fcntl(master, f2.F_SETFL, flags | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    def drain(timeout=0.8):
        data=b""
        end=time.time()+timeout
        while time.time()<end:
            r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.2)
            if r:
                try:
                    chunk=os.read(master, 65536)
                    if not chunk: break
                    data+=chunk
                    end=time.time()+0.3  # extend a bit after data
                except OSError: break
            # else continue until timeout
        return data
    init = drain(1.5)
    print(f"=== INIT len={len(init)} ===")
    print(repr(init))
    print()
    for k in keys:
        # k is bytes to send
        os.write(master, k)
        time.sleep(0.3)
        d = drain(0.8)
        print(f"=== after {repr(k)} len={len(d)} ===")
        print(repr(d))
        print()
    # cleanup
    try: p.terminate()
    except: pass
    try: p.wait(timeout=2)
    except: p.kill()
    os.close(master)
    return

# test simple prompt, typing, backspace, arrows
raw_session(["-p","hello world"], keys=[b"h", b"x", b"\x7f", b"e"])
PY"}

import subprocess, time

def tmux_run(cmd, width=80, height=24, wait=1.0):
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","-u","new-session","-d","-s","thokr","-x",str(width),"-y",str(height)], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr",cmd,"Enter"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(wait)
    return

def capture():
    r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t","thokr","-p","-e"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout

def send(k, literal=False):
    if literal:
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr","-l",k], capture_output=True)
    else:
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr",k], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)

def kill(): subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"], capture_output=True)

# Test key handling: backspace, esc, arrows, etc.
# Start with prompt "abc def"
tmux_run("./executable -p 'abc def'", width=80, height=24)
print("INIT:", repr(capture()))

# type 'a' then Backspace (BSpace), then check
send("a", literal=True)
print("after a:", repr(capture()))
send("BSpace")
print("after BSpace:", repr(capture()))

# left arrow should restart? README: press left to start over
send("Left")
print("after Left:", repr(capture()))
# type something then Right should give new prompt? but with custom prompt, Right should do nothing?
send("a", literal=True)
print("after a again:", repr(capture()))
send("Right")
print("after Right (custom prompt, should stay same?):", repr(capture()))

kill()
PY"}

import subprocess, time, shutil, pathlib
def tmux_run(cmd, width=100, height=30, wait=1.0):
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","-u","new-session","-d","-s","thokr","-x",str(width),"-y",str(height)], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr",cmd,"Enter"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(wait)
def capture():
    r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t","thokr","-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout
def send(k, literal=False):
    if literal:
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr","-l",k], capture_output=True)
    else:
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr",k], capture_output=True)

# longer prompt, constant speed
for delay in [0.2, 0.3]:
    shutil.rmtree("/tmp/thokr_long", ignore_errors=True)
    pathlib.Path("/tmp/thokr_long").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prompt="a"*20
    tmux_run(f"XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/thokr_long ./executable -p '{prompt}'", width=100, height=30)
    for k in list(prompt):
        send(k, literal=True)
        time.sleep(delay)
    time.sleep(1.5)
    log=open("/tmp/thokr_long/thokr/log.csv").read().strip().split("\n")[-1]
    print(f"delay {delay} log: {log}")
    print(capture().split("\n")[-8:-2])

subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"], capture_output=True)
PY"}

import subprocess, time, shutil, pathlib
def tmux_run(cmd, width=80, height=24, wait=1.0):
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","-u","new-session","-d","-s","thokr","-x",str(width),"-y",str(height)], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr",cmd,"Enter"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(wait)
def capture():
    r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t","thokr","-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout
def send(k, literal=False):
    if literal:
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr","-l",k], capture_output=True)
    else:
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr",k], capture_output=True)

shutil.rmtree("/tmp/thokr_t3", ignore_errors=True)
pathlib.Path("/tmp/thokr_t3").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
tmux_run(f"XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/thokr_t3 ./executable -p 'abcdefghij' -s 2", width=80, height=24, wait=1.0)
print("init:", repr(capture()))
time.sleep(4.0)
print("after timeout with no typing:", repr(capture()))
print(capture())
try:
    print(open("/tmp/thokr_t3/thokr/log.csv").read())
except Exception as e:
    print("log err", e)
subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"], capture_output=True)
PY

def tmux_run(cmd, width=80, height=24, wait=1.0):
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","-u","new-session","-d","-s","thokr","-x",str(width),"-y",str(height)], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr",cmd,"Enter"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(wait)
def capture():
    r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t","thokr","-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout
def capture_e():
    r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t","thokr","-p","-e"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout
def send(k, literal=False):
    if literal:
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr","-l",k], capture_output=True)
    else:
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr",k], capture_output=True)

    print(f"args {args} init:", repr(capture()[:200]))
    for k in list("ab"):
        send(k, literal=True)
        time.sleep(0.2)
    time.sleep(1.0)
    print(capture().split("\n")[-6:-2])
    try:
        print(open("/tmp/thokr_log/thokr/log.csv").read().strip().split("\n")[-1])
    except Exception as e:
        print(e)
    print("---")

subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"], capture_output=True)

def tmux_run(cmd, width=120, height=30, wait=1.0):
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","-u","new-session","-d","-s","thokr","-x",str(width),"-y",str(height)], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr",cmd,"Enter"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(wait)
def capture():
    r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t","thokr","-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout

# Sample word lists: collect many prompts for each language to build vocab
import collections
for lang in ["english", "english1k", "english10k"]:
    vocab=set()
    for i in range(20):
        tmux_run(f"./executable -w 15 -l {lang}", width=120, height=30, wait=0.8)
        txt=capture().strip()
        words=txt.split()
        vocab.update(words)
        subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"], capture_output=True)
    print(f"lang {lang} vocab size after 20x15: {len(vocab)} sample: {sorted(list(vocab))[:30]}")

import pty, os, subprocess, select, time, struct, fcntl, termios
master, slave = pty.openpty()
fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", 24, 80, 0, 0))
p = subprocess.Popen(["./executable","-p","hi"], stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, close_fds=True)
os.close(slave)
import fcntl as f2
flags = f2.fcntl(master, f2.F_GETFL)
f2.fcntl(master, f2.F_SETFL, flags | os.O_NONBLOCK)
def drain(timeout=1.0):
    data=b""
    end=time.time()+timeout
    while time.time()<end:
        r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.2)
        if r:
            try:
                chunk=os.read(master, 65536)
                if not chunk: break
                data+=chunk
                end=time.time()+0.3
            except OSError: break
    return data
print("init:", repr(drain(1.5)))
os.write(master, b"h")
time.sleep(0.3)
print("after h:", repr(drain(0.8)))
os.write(master, b"i")
time.sleep(0.5)
print("after i (results):", repr(drain(1.0)))
# send Escape
os.write(master, b"\x1b")
time.sleep(0.5)
print("after esc:", repr(drain(1.0)))
print("poll:", p.poll())
try: p.wait(timeout=2)
except: p.kill()
os.close(master)

            if r:
                try:
                    chunk=os.read(master, 65536)
                    if not chunk: break
                    data+=chunk
                    end=time.time()+0.2
                except OSError: break
        return data
    drain(1.0)

    time.sleep(0.4)
    d=drain(0.8)
    alive=p.poll() is None
    # determine: green/red/nothing/exit
    if not alive:

    elif b"38;5;2" in d:
        res="green(correct)"
    elif b"38;5;1" in d:
        res="red(wrong)"
    elif len(d)>30:
        res=f"other len{len(d)} {repr(d[:100])}"
    else:

    print(f"byte {hex(byte)} ({repr(chr(byte))}) -> {res}")
    try: p.terminate()
    except: pass
    try: p.wait(timeout=1)
    except: p.kill()
    os.close(master)

def get_words(args, width=400, height=80):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", height, width, 0, 0))
    p = subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, close_fds=True)
    os.close(slave)
    import fcntl as f2
    flags = f2.fcntl(master, f2.F_GETFL)
    f2.fcntl(master, f2.F_SETFL, flags | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    data=b""
    end=time.time()+1.0
    while time.time()<end:
        r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.15)
        if r:
            try:
                chunk=os.read(master, 65536)
                if not chunk: break
                data+=chunk
                end=time.time()+0.25
            except OSError: break
    try: p.terminate()
    except: pass
    try: p.wait(timeout=1)
    except: p.kill()

    txt = re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[a-zA-Z]', '', txt)

def jaro_winkler(s1, s2):
    if s1 == s2:
        return 1.0
    len1, len2 = len(s1), len(s2)
    if len1 == 0 or len2 == 0:
        return 0.0
    match_dist = max(len1, len2)//2 - 1
    if match_dist < 0:
        match_dist = 0
    s1_m = [False]*len1
    s2_m = [False]*len2
    matches = 0
    for i in range(len1):
        start = max(0, i-match_dist)
        end = min(i+match_dist+1, len2)
        for j in range(start, end):
            if not s2_m[j] and s1[i]==s2[j]:
                s1_m[i]=True
                s2_m[j]=True
                matches+=1

    k=0

def jaro_winkler(s1, s2):
    if s1 == s2:
        return 1.0
    len1, len2 = len(s1), len(s2)
    if len1 == 0 or len2 == 0:
        return 0.0
    match_dist = max(len1, len2)//2 - 1
    if match_dist < 0:
        match_dist = 0
    s1_m = [False]*len1
    s2_m = [False]*len2
    matches = 0
    for i in range(len1):
        start = max(0, i-match_dist)
        end = min(i+match_dist+1, len2)
        for j in range(start, end):
            if not s2_m[j] and s1[i]==s2[j]:
                s1_m[i]=True
                s2_m[j]=True
                matches+=1
                break
    if matches==0:
        return 0.0
    k=0
    trans=0
    for i in range(len1):
        if s1_m[i]:
            while not s2_m[k]:
                k+=1
            if s1[i]!=s2[k]:
                trans+=1
            k+=1
    trans//=2
    jaro=(matches/len1 + matches/len2 + (matches-trans)/matches)/3.0
    prefix=0
    for i in range(min(4, min(len1,len2))):
        if s1[i]==s2[i]:
            prefix+=1
        else:
            break
    return jaro + prefix*0.1*(1-jaro)

import subprocess, time, shutil, pathlib
def tmux_run(cmd, width=80, height=24, wait=1.0):
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","-u","new-session","-d","-s","thokr","-x",str(width),"-y",str(height)], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr",cmd,"Enter"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(wait)
def capture():
    r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t","thokr","-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout
def send(k, literal=False):
    if literal:
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr","-l",k], capture_output=True)
    else:
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr",k], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.4)

shutil.rmtree("/tmp/thokr_cmp2", ignore_errors=True)
pathlib.Path("/tmp/thokr_cmp2").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
tmux_run(f"XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/thokr_cmp2 /tmp/new_exec -p 'hello'", width=80, height=24, wait=1.0)
print("init:", repr(capture()))
for k in list("hello"):
    send(k, literal=True)
    print(f"after {k}:", repr(capture()[:300]))
time.sleep(1.5)
print("results:", repr(capture()))
print(capture())
subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"], capture_output=True)
PY"}

    time.sleep(0.3)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","-u","new-session","-d","-s","thokr","-x",str(width),"-y",str(height)], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr",cmd,"Enter"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(wait)
def capture():
    r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t","thokr","-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout
def capture_e():
    r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t","thokr","-p","-e"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout
def send(k, literal=False):
    if literal:
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr","-l",k], capture_output=True)
    else:
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr",k], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.2)

# Use fixed custom multi-line prompt that wraps: 20x word (99 chars, wraps to 2 lines at 80)
prompt=" ".join(["word"]*5)  # 5 words, 24 chars? Actually "word "*5 = 24? 5*4+4=24, fits in one line (70 usable), single-line. Need longer to wrap: 20 words (99 chars) wraps to 2 lines.
prompt=" ".join(["word"]*20)
for exe in ["/tmp/new_exec2"]:
    shutil.rmtree("/tmp/thokr_multi", ignore_errors=True)
    pathlib.Path("/tmp/thokr_multi").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    for k in list(prompt[:10]):

    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"], capture_output=True)

import subprocess, time, shutil, pathlib
def tmux_run(cmd, width=80, height=24, wait=1.0):
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","-u","new-session","-d","-s","thokr","-x",str(width),"-y",str(height)], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr",cmd,"Enter"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(wait)
def capture():
    r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t","thokr","-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout
def capture_e():
    r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t","thokr","-p","-e"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout
def send(k, literal=False):
    if literal:
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr","-l",k], capture_output=True)
    else:
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","thokr",k], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)

# Test Backspace, Left, Right for new vs orig (single-line)
for exe in ["./executable","/tmp/newest"]:
    print(f"=== {exe} Backspace/Left/Right ===")
    tmux_run(f"{exe} -p 'hello'", width=80, height=24, wait=0.8)
    print("init:", repr(capture()[:100]))
    send("h", literal=True)
    send("e", literal=True)
    print("after he:", repr(capture()[:100]), repr(capture_e()[:500]))
    send("BSpace")
    print("after BSpace:", repr(capture()[:100]))
    send("e", literal=True)
    print("after e again:", repr(capture()[:100]))
    send("Left")
    print("after Left (restart):", repr(capture()[:100]))
    send("h", literal=True)
    print("after h post-left:", repr(capture()[:100]))
    send("Right")
    print("after Right (new):", repr(capture()[:200]))
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"], capture_output=True)
PY"}

But we haven't overwritten yet. For fair compare, run via python3 thokr.py but normalize prog name in output (replace thokr.py with executable)
    quoted=" ".join(shlex.quote(a) for a in args)
    # Use thokr.py directly (prog will be thokr.py)
    r=subprocess.run(f"python3 thokr.py {quoted}", shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
    # normalize prog name in outputs: replace thokr.py with executable
    out=r.stdout.replace("thokr.py","executable")
    err=r.stderr.replace("thokr.py","executable")
    return r.returncode, out, err
